article.title: 阅读四 · 正式英语的衰落
article.background: 文化与语言评论。既呈现作者对正式语言之美消逝的惋惜，也保留语言学家对语言自然变化的克制与反讽。

sentences.en: Americans no longer expect public figures, whether in speech or in writing, to command the English language with skill and gift.
sentences.zh: 美国人如今已不再期待公众人物无论说话还是写作都能娴熟而富有才华地驾驭英语。
prosody_focus: Americans no longer expect public figures, whether in speech or in writing, to c

segments.text: Americans no longer expect public figures, whether in speech or in writing, to command the English language with skill and gift.

sentences.en: Nor do they aspire to such command themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己也不再追求这种语言驾驭力。
prosody_focus: Nor do they aspire to such command themselves.

segments.text: Nor do they aspire to such command themselves.

sentences.en: In his latest book, Doing Our Own Thing: The Degradation of Language and Music and Why We Should, Like, Care, John McWhorter, a linguist and controversialist of mixed liberal and conservative views, sees the triumph of 1960s counter-culture as responsible for the decline of formal English.
sentences.zh: 语言学家兼争议评论者约翰·麦克沃特在新书《各行其是：语言与音乐的退化，以及我们为何——嗯——应当在意》中，把正式英语的衰落归因于20世纪60年代反主流文化的胜利。

segments.text: In his latest book, Doing Our Own Thing: The Degradation of Language and Music and Why We Should, Like, Care, John McWhorter, a linguist and controversialist of mixed liberal and conservative views, sees the triumph of 1960s counter-culture as responsible for the decline of formal English.

sentences.en: Blaming the permissive 1960s is nothing new, but this is not yet another criticism against the decline in education.
sentences.zh: 把问题归咎于宽纵的60年代并不新鲜，但这并不是又一篇批评教育衰退的老生常谈。
prosody_focus: Blaming the permissive 1960s is nothing new, but this is not yet another critici

segments.text: Blaming the permissive 1960s is nothing new, but this is not yet another criticism against the decline in education.

sentences.en: Mr. McWhorter’s academic speciality is language history and change, and he sees the gradual disappearance of “whom”, for example, to be natural and no more regrettable than the loss of the case-endings of Old English.
sentences.zh: 麦克沃特的学术专长是语言史与语言变化；例如，他认为“whom”的逐渐消失十分自然，并不比古英语格尾的消失更值得惋惜。

segments.text: Mr. McWhorter’s academic speciality is language history and change, and he sees the gradual disappearance of “whom”, for example, to be natural and no more regrettable than the loss of the case-endings of Old English.

sentences.en: But the cult of the authentic and the personal, “doing our own thing”, has spelt the death of formal speech, writing, poetry and music.
sentences.zh: 然而，对“真实”和“个性”的崇拜，也就是“各行其是”，却宣告了正式演说、写作、诗歌与音乐的死亡。
prosody_focus: But the cult of the authentic and the personal, “doing our own thing”, has spelt

segments.text: But the cult of the authentic and the personal, “doing our own thing”, has spelt the death of formal speech, writing, poetry and music.

sentences.en: While even the modestly educated sought an elevated tone when they put pen to paper before the 1960s, even the most well-regarded writing since then has sought to capture spoken English on the page.
sentences.zh: 在60年代以前，即便受教育程度一般的人落笔时也会追求庄重语调；而此后，即使最受推崇的作品也往往试图把口语直接搬到纸面上。

segments.text: While even the modestly educated sought an elevated tone when they put pen to paper before the 1960s, even the most well-regarded writing since then has sought to capture spoken English on the page.

sentences.en: Equally, in poetry, the highly personal, performative genre is the only form that could claim real liveliness.
sentences.zh: 诗歌也是如此：高度个人化、强调表演性的体裁，几乎成了唯一还能称得上有活力的形式。
prosody_focus: Equally, in poetry, the highly personal, performative genre is the only form tha

segments.text: Equally, in poetry, the highly personal, performative genre is the only form that could claim real liveliness.

sentences.en: In both oral and written English, talking is triumphing over speaking, spontaneity over craft.
sentences.zh: 无论口头还是书面英语，“闲谈”正在压倒“演说”，即兴正在压倒技艺。
prosody_focus: In both oral and written English, talking is triumphing over speaking, spontanei

segments.text: In both oral and written English, talking is triumphing over speaking, spontaneity over craft.

sentences.en: Illustrated with an entertaining array of examples from both high and low culture, the trend that Mr. McWhorter documents is unmistakable.
sentences.zh: 麦克沃特从高雅文化和通俗文化中列举了大量生动有趣的例子，他所记录的趋势清晰得无可否认。

segments.text: Illustrated with an entertaining array of examples from both high and low culture, the trend that Mr. McWhorter documents is unmistakable.

sentences.en: But it is less clear, to take the question of his subtitle, why we should, like, care.
sentences.zh: 可借用他副标题里的口吻来说，我们究竟为什么要“嗯，在意”这件事，就没那么清楚了。

segments.text: But it is less clear, to take the question of his subtitle, why we should, like, care.

sentences.en: As a linguist, he acknowledges that all varieties of human language, including non-standard ones like Black English, can be powerfully expressive — there exists no language or dialect in the world that cannot convey complex ideas.
sentences.zh: 作为语言学家，他承认人类语言的各种变体，包括黑人英语这样的非标准形式，都具有强大的表达力；世界上不存在无法表达复杂思想的语言或方言。

segments.text: As a linguist, he acknowledges that all varieties of human language, including non-standard ones like Black English, can be powerfully expressive — there exists no language or dialect in the world that cannot convey complex ideas.

sentences.en: He is not arguing, as many do, that we can no longer think straight because we do not talk proper.
sentences.zh: 他并不像许多人那样声称，因为我们说话不够规范，所以连思路也不再清楚。

segments.text: He is not arguing, as many do, that we can no longer think straight because we do not talk proper.

sentences.en: Russians have a deep love for their own language and carry large chunks of memorized poetry in their heads, while Italian politicians tend to elaborate speech that would seem old-fashioned to most English-speakers.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人深爱自己的语言，脑中能背下大段诗歌；意大利政治人物则偏爱华丽繁复的演说，在大多数英语使用者听来甚至有些古旧。

segments.text: Russians have a deep love for their own language and carry large chunks of memorized poetry in their heads, while Italian politicians tend to elaborate speech that would seem old-fashioned to most English-speakers.

sentences.en: Mr. McWhorter acknowledges that formal language is not strictly necessary, and proposes no radical education reforms — he is really grieving over the loss of something beautiful more than useful.
sentences.zh: 麦克沃特承认正式语言并非绝对必需，也没有提出激进的教育改革；与其说他在哀叹某种有用之物的消失，不如说是在惋惜一种美的逝去。

segments.text: Mr. McWhorter acknowledges that formal language is not strictly necessary, and proposes no radical education reforms — he is really grieving over the loss of something beautiful more than useful.

sentences.en: We now take our English “on paper plates instead of china”.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们享用英语，仿佛从精美瓷器换成了纸盘。
prosody_focus: We now take our English “on paper plates instead of china”.

segments.text: We now take our English “on paper plates instead of china”.

sentences.en: A shame, perhaps, but probably an inevitable one.
sentences.zh: 这也许令人惋惜，却很可能无可避免。
